title: REPORT on the European Semester for economic policy coordination: employment and social priorities – annual report 2026
part_text: 20. Strongly believes that an individual right to training for workers during working hours, which addresses the main barriers to pursuing training, can ensure quality upskilling and reskilling, employee training and career development support in order to ensure a predictable and stable supply of skilled workers for employers; stresses the need for tackling the cost barrier by ensuring cost-free training for workers, supported by funding, tax incentives and partnerships; stresses that the right to training must explicitly include mandatory, high-quality, regular and paid occupational health and safety training aimed at preventing workplace accidents, occupational diseases and deaths at work, including in high-risk sectors; recalls that all training courses must be adapted to the specific tasks performed and to the risks of each sector, and must be provided in a language and format that all workers can understand, including workers in subcontracting chains, temporary agency workers and migrant workers; stresses that national institutions and social partners are responsible for the training of employees, and highlights their essential role in the implementation of the right to training; calls, in this regard, on Member States to prioritise and promote training schemes developed jointly by workers and their employers, ensuring that upskilling and reskilling respond to real market demand and contribute to career progression; recalls that training must never be used to shift responsibility away from employers, who remain fully responsible for ensuring safe and healthy workplaces through prevention measures, adequate staffing, proper work organisation and compliance with occupational health and safety rules; calls on the Commission to explore and issue guidance on how public-private partnerships between Member States and enterprises can fund the training, reskilling and upskilling of workers, in particular the right to training for individual workers;
